title: Adequacy of sstriple by case split on the four continuations
intent: Reduce the headline adequacy theorem -- a Hoare triple (sstriple) over the non-deterministic evaluator implies the post-condition for every possible continuation -- to a case split on the four continuation constructors: Success, Return and Abort are dispatched to the three per-constructor adequacy lemmas, and Yield is discharged as impossible by deep_evaluate_basic_no_yield'.

parent.name: sstriple_adequacy
parent.statement:
lemma sstriple_adequacy:
  assumes \<open>\<Gamma> ; \<xi> \<turnstile> e \<stileturn> \<phi> \<bowtie> \<rho> \<bowtie> \<theta>\<close>
      and \<open>\<sigma> \<Turnstile> \<xi>\<close>
      and \<open>c \<in> deep_evaluates_nondet_basic (yield_handler \<Gamma>) e \<sigma>\<close>
    shows \<open>case c of
            continuation.Success v \<sigma>' \<Rightarrow> \<sigma>' \<Turnstile> \<phi> v
          | continuation.Return v \<sigma>' \<Rightarrow> \<sigma>' \<Turnstile> \<rho> v
          | continuation.Abort a \<sigma>' \<Rightarrow> \<sigma>' \<Turnstile> \<theta> a
          | continuation.Yield _ _ _ \<Rightarrow> False\<close>

children.name: atriple_rel_eval_value_adequacy
children.statement:
lemma atriple_rel_eval_value_adequacy:
  assumes \<open>\<xi> \<turnstile> eval_value Y e \<stileturn>\<^sub>R \<phi>\<close>
      and \<open>\<sigma> \<Turnstile> \<xi>\<close>
      and \<open>continuation.Success v \<sigma>' \<in> deep_evaluates_nondet_basic Y e \<sigma>\<close>
    shows \<open>\<sigma>' \<Turnstile> \<phi> v\<close>
children.closed_by: using assms by (auto simp add: atriple_rel_def eval_value_def urust_eval_predicate_defs)

children.name: deep_evaluate_basic_no_yield'
children.statement:
lemma deep_evaluate_basic_no_yield':
  shows \<open>Yield \<pi> \<sigma>' e' \<in> deep_evaluates_nondet_basic y e \<sigma> \<longleftrightarrow> False\<close>

applicability.goal_shape: a goal `case c of Success v \<sigma>' \<Rightarrow> ... | Return v \<sigma>' \<Rightarrow> ... | Abort a \<sigma>' \<Rightarrow> ... | Yield _ _ _ \<Rightarrow> False` where `c` is drawn from `deep_evaluates_nondet_basic` over a finite continuation datatype, and the hypothesis is a defined relation (here `sstriple`, a conjunction of three `atriple_rel` exact triples) that already packages one fact per constructor
applicability.use_when: the result type has finitely many constructors (here four: Success, Return, Abort, Yield); one per-constructor adequacy lemma already exists for each 'real' constructor; and a separate lemma rules out the remaining constructor (here Yield), so the `split: continuation.splits` is exhaustive by construction of the datatype and no disjunction lemma needs to be stated
applicability.avoid_when: the per-constructor lemmas have not yet been stated (then the split leaves goals that `auto` must solve from raw definitions, which may not close); the constructor count is large; or the case for a constructor genuinely holds rather than being impossible (then a real child lemma is needed instead of a falsity lemma)

claims.claim: The parent sstriple_adequacy is closed by a single `auto` call (lines 63-66) that unfolds sstriple_def, splits on continuation.splits, and dispatches the four continuation constructors to the four named direct lemmas deep_evaluate_basic_no_yield', atriple_rel_eval_value_adequacy, atriple_rel_eval_return_adequacy and atriple_rel_eval_abort_adequacy; the theory is built by the project's CI.
claims.evidence: https://github.com/awslabs/AutoCorrode/blob/200f1acf2d264f2dedee33792b986ebe73c224a3/Shallow_Separation_Logic/Adequacy.thy#L63-L66; .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `isabelle build -b -d . AutoCorrode`, the AutoCorrode session lists Shallow_Separation_Logic, and Shallow_Separation_Logic/ROOT lists Adequacy as its first theory

claims.claim: The three per-constructor children close on their own by unfolding definitions only -- `using assms by (auto simp add: atriple_rel_def eval_value_def urust_eval_predicate_defs)` (line 36) and the analogous eval_return/eval_abort forms (lines 43, 50) -- with no further project lemma; the fourth child deep_evaluate_basic_no_yield' closes from its named sibling deep_evaluate_basic_no_yield by `force` (line 79).

direct_lemmas = 4; glue_lines = 14 (Adequacy.thy lines 53-66, the full lemma); child proof lines = 6 (value, 31-36), 6 (return, 38-43), 6 (abort, 45-50), 3 (no_yield', 77-79); depth = 3, the longest chain of project lemmas below the main theorem: sstriple_adequacy -> deep_evaluate_basic_no_yield' -> deep_evaluate_basic_no_yield -> expression_wf_base_is_wf.

The authors state the adequacy goal and the Yield side in the surrounding text: 'from a Hoare triple/weakest precondition entailment/function contract on a program e we can derive that the evaluating e on appropriate machines does not go wrong' (lines 12-16), and 'Evaluating with deep_evaluates_nondet_basic will never terminate in Yield' (the comment at line 62).

The same `split: continuation.splits` case-split move recurs four more times in the same file -- contract_adequacy (line 92), wp_adequacy_deterministic (line 111), sstriple_from_evaluation (line 141), contract_from_evaluation (line 163) -- and sstriple_adequacy itself is reused as the head of the two corollaries wp_adequacy (line 77) and contract_adequacy (line 92).

metrics.how_counted: glue_lines = lines 53-66 of Adequacy.thy (the full lemma sstriple_adequacy; the proof body `using assms by (auto ... split: continuation.splits)` is lines 63-66); direct_lemmas = the four named lemmas the auto call cites; depth = longest project-lemma chain sstriple_adequacy -> deep_evaluate_basic_no_yield' -> deep_evaluate_basic_no_yield -> expression_wf_base_is_wf; children_closed_by_automation = all four children close by a single auto/force call

consequences: The case split produces one goal per constructor plus an exhaustiveness obligation that `continuation.splits` (a datatype case rule) discharges itself, exactly because `continuation` is a datatype. The Yield case is not 'covered' but ruled out by deep_evaluate_basic_no_yield', so the decomposition relies on that lemma's strength (`Yield ... \<longleftrightarrow> False`). If a new constructor were added to the `continuation` datatype, the split would produce a new goal and `auto` would fail to close it, exposing the exhaustiveness obligation.
